text: and OSI installed and configured the OSI Monarch system along with the DERMS applications: integraDERMS and DERComms. • IntegraDERMS is the core DERMS application that is installed on a dedicated server that is responsible for all the main core DER functions like estimation, optimization and scheduling. • DERComms is an OSI Monarch web-application that is installed on a dedicated OpenADR server to communicate with aggregators. The team upgraded the baseline product versions to an upcoming version that is currently in the OSI research and development (R&D) phase of their product roadmap. This R&D version enables more use-cases for testing, such as OpenADR messages and near real-time telemetry, for finer tuned dispatch and reporting. These updated product versions also allowed for a number of issue fixes and support features. 6.1.8.1.3.1 DERMS Sandbox and Set Up To configure the DERMS sandbox, there were a number of DERMS model workshops conducted between OSI, PAC, and EPE to capture all the use-cases and necessary project data requirements. OSI provided a framework for DER definition and boundary conditions that made for easy ingestion into their system for modeling. The project 20 team worked to assemble all of the required data (nameplate values, control windows, feeder and substation information, locational data, etc.) on the controllable DERs into the required format for upload and configuration into the OSI system. Using this, OSI was able to model those DERs in the DERMS database with primary goal to start modelling USU DERs. 6.1.8.1.3.2 Control Communications Schema To prepare for end-to-end communications and controls, OSI, USU and PAC set up OpenADR communications between the OSI pull-VTN (DERComms) and PAC pull-VEN as referenced earlier. Since OSI only supports the pull method of OpenADR and PacifiCorp has strict cyber security requirements to only allow for the use of OpenADR with the push method, PAC developed a pull to push converter that was previously explained. OSI Webplatform has number of cyber security requirements, including SSL certificates and API token, that necessitated a number of design meetings to come up with solution for the integrations with PAC. The appropriate security requirements were implemented for the integration between the PAC VEN and OSI VTN. After successfully testing communications between PAC VEN and OSI VTN, the team conducted a deep dive on specific reports requirements and have successfully implemented and tested the reports listed below and as outlined in the OSI OpenADR implementation guide. • TELEMETRY_STATUS • TELEMETRY_USGAE • FORECASTED_FLEXIBILITY The team successfully implemented and tested the OpenADR controls using OadrDistribute event by sending real power setpoints. The project team also ran simulated events to each group of DERs to test the end-to-end communications between PAC and the components of the microgrid through the OpenADR VEN.
